overclaims.statement: Kristalina Georgieva was mentioned as a Bulgarian candidate for UN Secretary General in 2016, though not the frontrunner.
overclaims.citedQuote: There really is one genuinely eligible Bulgarian frontrunner for the position of UN Secretary General, and it isn't Kristalina Georgieva .
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage says there is one genuinely eligible Bulgarian frontrunner 'and it isn't Kristalina Georgieva.' That establishes she was not the frontrunner but does not state that she was mentioned as a candidate at all; the candidate framing is inferred beyond the passage.

Presented in the career section with no time qualifier, 'chief of the World Bank' reads as a current or head-of-institution role. She was Chief Executive Officer of the World Bank 2017-2019 (with a ~three-month acting presidency) and has led the IMF since October 2019, so an unqualified 'chief of the World Bank' overstates the role and its currency. This aligns with the listed unjustified conclusion about presenting her World Bank office as current.

overclaims.statement: Her current term expires on September 30.
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage is from a March 2024 article about her first term expiring September 30, 2024. The dossier elsewhere records that she began a second five-year term on 1 October 2024, so reproducing 'her current term expires on September 30' from the older article presents a superseded fact as current.

overclaims.statement: Georgieva stated she would be honored to serve a second five-year term if renominated.
overclaims.citedQuote: I would be honored to continue to serve as the IMF Managing Director
overclaims.rationale: The cited passage reads 'I would be honored to continue to serve as the IMF Managing Director.' It does not mention a second five-year term or renomination conditions; those specifics are added beyond what the quoted passage supports.

usefulness.rationale: The dossier gives a clear, well-sourced picture: who Georgieva is (Bulgarian economist, b. 1953, Sofia), her career arc (World Bank from 1993, European Commissioner 2010-2016, World Bank CEO 2017-2019 including a three-month interim presidency, IMF MD since 1 Oct 2019 and into a second term from Oct 2024), the 2021 data-rigging allegation with her denial, and current work (Argentina/Milei engagement, Ukraine visit, CBDC advocacy, fiscal warnings). A reader could realistically prepare for a meeting: current role, recent positions, key counterparts, and sensitive topics are all covered. It falls short of full marks on epistemic honesty: uncertainty is conveyed only through per-claim status labels (contested/unknown/stale) rather than any explicit statement of what the dossier does not know, and it draws on some low-quality sources (a 'Great Reset' video, tag pages) without flagging their reliability.
